extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers and stakeholders interested in labor relations, policy makers, and parties to the GM–UAW dispute
extracted.subtask_description: A newspaper report reproducing the Fact-Finding Board statement and General Motors' formal position explaining reasons for withdrawing from fact-finding, and outlining standards, procedural expectations, and policy arguments relevant to wage determination. Targets readers following the GM–UAW dispute and national labor policy issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fact-Finding Board obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: The obligation of the fact-finding board is to develop, to the best of its ability, the facts relevant to the General Motors–U.A.W. dispute, and to submit these facts to the President, with such recommendations as the board may deem appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To do this as thoroughly and reliably as the President and the public have a right to expect, the board needs the wholehearted co-operation of both parties; without cooperation the board can either report inability to proceed or do the very best it can on the evidence available. The board must follow the latter alternative when so charged by the President.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for cooperation of both parties
rubrics_metrics.description: The board needs the whole-hearted co-operation of both parties to the dispute; without the co-operation of both sides, the board has only two alternatives — either to report to the President that they were unable to proceed, or to do the very best we can on the basis of evidence that is or will be available to us.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cooperation affects whether fact-finding can proceed fully; lack of cooperation may limit the investigation's scope and the confidence parties and the public place in the board's findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to pay is a factor but not controlling
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability to pay will not be regarded as the only or controlling factor in determining the amount of a fair and equitable wage adjustment. The board is not concerned with fixing profits but only with the question of what is a fair wage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The board continues to treat ability to pay as one factor among others (earnings, costs, equities) rather than the sole determinant of wage increases; this position aligns with Presidential guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board may request particular company financial information
rubrics_metrics.description: The board has requested particular information relevant to these matters and may later ask to examine particular books or records in accordance with the President's Statement of Dec. 20.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If such an examination is requested the information would be kept confidential in accordance with the President's statement. The board will determine as the case develops whether examination of specific records is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to satisfy wage‑price policy and avoid inflationary consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: The board is obliged by the President's wage-price policy to satisfy itself that any wage adjustment which it may recommend will not, if adopted, have inflationary price consequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The board cannot exercise this duty without a reasonably adequate picture of the company's financial situation; assessing inflationary impact requires sufficient financial information and considered judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of forecasts and estimates in measuring ability to pay
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed measures of ability to pay involve forecasts, assumptions and estimates regarding future costs, profits, demand, expenditures and expansion plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forecasts and estimates (e.g., projected take-home pay, expansion expenditures of hundreds of millions) are proper factors to consider but require careful scrutiny because they are inherently uncertain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of investigation must be judiciously limited
rubrics_metrics.description: The scope of the board's investigation will be so limited as the board determines appropriate; decisions about examining confidential materials and the depth of inquiry involve judgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The board must balance the need for information (to meet Presidential policy and public confidence) against confidentiality and relevance; judgments on scope are to be made as the case develops.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of requested information
rubrics_metrics.description: If the board requests examination of company books or records, the information would be kept confidential in accordance with the President's Statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confidential handling of company financial evidence is pledged to encourage submission, but confidentiality does not eliminate the board's need to rely on such evidence to check inflationary effects and fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board's use of a wide range of evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: The board will sift as carefully and objectively as possible the available evidence, including governmental data, the transcript of the extensive negotiations between the parties, and the various reply briefs and submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determinations about a fair wage should rest on customary tests applied to the nature of the case, with evidence weighed in conjunction with other factors as warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Company may withdraw if procedural/standpoint conditions unacceptable
rubrics_metrics.description: The General Motors Corporation feels that it has no choice but to withdraw from these proceedings, unless and until the board, on further consideration, should decide that under the peculiar circumstances of this case, ability to pay is not a proper factor for its consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A party's withdrawal is presented as justified where it believes the board's procedural posture or standards (e.g., refusal to treat ability to pay appropriately) prevent good‑faith fact-finding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fair wage determination is not only arithmetic; may implicate national policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The issue is not one of arithmetic or facts in the books of the corporation to settle; it is an issue of national policy that properly belongs to Congress rather than solely to fact‑finding bodies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GM argues that questions involving wages, prices, and profits on an industry-wide basis transcend ordinary fact-finding and raise ideological and policy questions beyond the board's competence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of encroachment on management judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: The union's proposals seek to enter the very heart of management judgment and discretion in private industry and would persuade the Fact-Finding Board to do likewise—encroachment heretofore exercised only by regulatory bodies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statement warns that allowing fact-finding or unions to intrude on managerial decisions (paying presidents, choosing directors, management duties) would undermine private management prerogatives and regulatory boundaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anti‑trust and competition concerns if unions bargain over prices/profits
rubrics_metrics.description: If national unions are permitted to bargain with employers on prices or profit margins, this area of competition and consumer protection will be removed; such combinations have been condemned by the Supreme Court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Industry-wide bargaining that controls wages, prices and marketing would risk violating antitrust principles and reduce competition, harming consumers and the market system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Union ultimatum undermines fact‑finding function
rubrics_metrics.description: The union has served notice on the Fact-Finding Board that no action by the board short of adoption of its position will be accepted; it says 'We will make no compromise... We will stand on that position.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A rigid ultimatum which refuses compromise or acceptance of fact-finding outcomes threatens to render fact-finding futile; the board's independence and ability to recommend compromises depend on parties' willingness to accept recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tests of fairness and equity should be applied in wage determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: Customary tests applied to determine what is a fair and equitable wage include comparisons with competitors, earnings, take-home pay, cost-of-living adjustments and other contextual factors; the test of fairness and equity should not be rejected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The board and parties should weigh facts and figures (earnings, take-home pay, industry comparators) alongside policy considerations; rejecting equity tests undermines reasoned settlement.
